name: Theertha International Artists' Collective
funding: Arts Collaboratory, Prince Claus Fund, Triangle Network, artist self-management; registered non-profit trust.

name: Tikhaya Studio
funding: Artist-run autonomous non-profit founded 2015 by Artem Filatov; grants, ticket/catalogue sales and donated artworks; a Garage Museum grant funds its archive.
watch: Nine resident artists; collaborates with Garage on archiving the Nizhny Novgorod scene.
records_note: This artist-run studio's site names its team and takes donations but posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board.

name: Tjibaou Cultural Centre (ADCK)
funding: Operating budget about 400M XPF (~US$3.6M) in 2026. Run by the public agency ADCK; the French State pays 68% of a 405M XPF renovation (2025).
watch: Renzo Piano building from 1998, run by the Kanak culture agency ADCK. It is being renovated through 2027 and stays open during the works.
records_note: The centre's site carries no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; the 2026 budget and State renovation share come only from press coverage.

name: Toi Māori Aotearoa
funding: Small charitable trust; major funder is Creative New Zealand (government and Lotteries money); runs the Toi Māori Gallery.
watch: Māori arts trust and artists' network founded in 1996; mainly a service body with a small gallery and shop.
records_note: Annual reports 2018 to 2025 carry financial statements; the 2025 report names Creative New Zealand as core funder with partner acknowledgements and lists the trustees.

name: Tokyo Arts and Space
funding: Its 2026 shows are run and paid for by the Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture (Tokyo government). The Korean Embassy and Cultural Center back one show.
watch: As Tokyo Wonder Site (2006-07), it was at the centre of a nepotism row over Governor Ishihara's son's paid role, raised in the Tokyo assembly.
records_note: Its operator, the Tokyo history and culture foundation, posts reports for FY2017 to FY2025, accounts for FY2020 to FY2025, a board list and named donors.

name: Trafó House of Contemporary Arts
funding: Municipality of Budapest, International Visegrad Fund, Creative Europe; independent municipal cultural institution.

name: Tramway
watch: Glasgow Life's 2025/26 thanks list includes Bloomberg Philanthropies; 260 UK artists asked five London theatres to drop Bloomberg in May 2026. Not targeted here.
records_note: Managed by Glasgow Life, which posts annual reviews 2013-14 to 2025-26, charity accounts, a supporters list for 2025/26 and its board.

name: transmediale
funding: Annual festival (2026) funded since 2004 by the Kulturstiftung des Bundes. Berlin Senate, bpb, Medienboard and Creative Europe funding was listed for 2020–21.
watch: Coordinates mark central Berlin, because festival venues change each year. Its 2026 partner programmes include the Schering Stiftung and HAU.
records_note: transmediale names no board and posts no reports or accounts; its old partner page shows funder logos and its about page names two funders.

name: tranzit.cz / Matter of Art Biennale
funding: Ministry of Culture Czech Republic, Prague City Hall, ERSTE Foundation; non-profit foundation grant model, 0% fossil fuel support.

name: tranzit.ro
funding: ERSTE Foundation, AFCN (Administration of the National Cultural Fund Romania); independent non-profit association.
watch: Decentralized, self-governing collective platform in Bucharest, Cluj, and Iași; critical pedagogy and social movements.

name: Triangle-Astérides, centre d'art contemporain
funding: Ministère de la Culture (DRAC PACA), Ville de Marseille, Région Sud, Département des Bouches-du-Rhône; non-profit association.
watch: Non-profit contemporary art centre and residency within La Friche; founding member of Triangle Network.

name: Triple Canopy
funding: National Endowment for the Arts (NEA), NYSCA, DCLA, Andy Warhol Foundation; 501(c)(3) non-profit publisher.
watch: Non-profit magazine and project space covering digital culture, labor and public discourse.
